landing.heroKicker: Crop advisory for India’s small farms
landing.heroTitle: Advice that knows your soil, your sky and your mandi
landing.heroLead: Fieldwise turns a Soil Health Card, the week’s weather and nearby mandi prices into clear, local advice in Hindi and English.

kharif.name: Kharif
kharif.body: Monsoon rain sets the plan. Fieldwise scores each crop against your soil and the water you will actually get, and warns when humid spells bring fungus.

rabi.name: Rabi
rabi.body: Mustard and wheat on stored moisture. Irrigation is planned day by day from crop water use, so every watering counts.

zaid.name: Zaid
zaid.body: Short, hot and dry. Quick crops, careful water and spray days picked for calm, rain-free mornings.

landing.soilTitle: Your Soil Health Card, read layer by layer
landing.soilBody: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium decide how much urea, DAP and potash a field needs. Fieldwise adjusts every dose to your card: more where a nutrient is low, less where it is high.
landing.soilNote: Particle density shows an example card: sparse is low, dense is high.
landing.waterTitle: Irrigate on the right day, not every day
landing.waterBody: A daily soil-water balance from the live forecast tells farmers when the soil has used up its safe store, and how many millimetres to give.
landing.mandiTitle: From field to the best mandi
landing.mandiBody: Prices in four nearby mandis, the week’s trend and MSP side by side, with plain sell-or-hold advice.
landing.numbersNote: Counts come from the running demo database.
landing.mapTitle: Ten districts, every major soil and climate
landing.mapBody: From the arid west to the delta east, black regur to red laterite: the pilot covers the conditions most Indian smallholders farm in.
landing.ctaTitle: Bring the extension officer to every phone
landing.ctaBody: Farmers ask, officers answer and alert, and the advice keeps working when the network does not.
landing.footer: Smart India Hackathon prototype. Agronomic figures are indicative. Mandi prices are simulated unless an Agmarknet key is configured.
landing.stillNote: Showing still images: reduced motion or Lite mode is on.
landing.cropsBody: Fieldwise scores each crop against your soil, water and weather, then plans its fertiliser, irrigation and sale.

pitch.title: Fieldwise pitch
pitch.controls: Arrow keys, space or a clicker to move. F for full screen. P opens presenter notes.
pitch.simulated: Mandi prices in the demo are simulated.

problem.title: 86% of India’s farms are under 2 hectares. Advice reaches few of them.
points: One extension officer for roughly a thousand farm families
Soil Health Cards are issued, but rarely turned into a fertiliser plan
Weather and mandi prices arrive late, in the wrong language, or not at all
problem.notes: Open with the farmer, not the tech. A smallholder in Nagpur has a Soil Health Card in a drawer, a phone in her pocket, and no one to turn the two into a decision. Keep this under a minute.

solution.title: Your soil, your sky, your mandi, in one clear plan
points: Crops scored for this field and this season, with reasons
Urea, DAP and potash in bags and rupees, adjusted to the Soil Health Card
Irrigation days from a live forecast, and sell-or-hold advice from nearby mandis
solution.notes: Three inputs the farmer already has, one plan she can act on today. Everything works in Hindi and English, and the advice engine reproduces the field-tested formulas exactly.

demo.title: Ask a question on the phone. Watch it land on the officer’s desk.
points: Sign in as the farmer, choose a crop, check a leaf photo
Ask the extension officer; the answer arrives in real time
The officer sends a district alert to every farmer growing that crop
demo.notes: Switch to the app (Alt+Tab). Farmer: planner, choose a crop, health photo check. Ask a question. Officer window: it appears live, reply. Back to the farmer: the answer and a celebration. The counters on this slide update as you go.

impact.title: Less guesswork on every acre
points: Fertiliser matched to the soil instead of a blanket dose
Water only on the days the soil needs it
Better prices by choosing the mandi and the moment
impact.notes: Be honest: these are the levers, not measured outcomes yet. A pilot with one Krishi Vigyan Kendra would measure input cost per acre and price realised. Point at the live numbers.

architecture.title: Built to run on a ₹8,000 phone and a free-tier server
points: React app, installable and readable offline; 3D only where the device can take it
Fastify API with the shared advisory engine, Prisma on SQLite or Postgres
Live forecast from Open-Meteo, Agmarknet prices with a key, Socket.IO for alerts
architecture.notes: Follow a packet: the phone asks the API, the engine scores crops, weather comes from Open-Meteo and is cached for an hour, alerts go out over sockets. If any outside service fails, the app says so and keeps working with labelled simulated data.

roadmap.title: From ten districts to a state
points: Next 3 months: pilot with one KVK, Marathi, Tamil and Odia, SMS and IVR alerts
Next 6 months: a trained PlantVillage leaf model running on the phone
Next 12 months: state rollout through the agriculture department’s extension staff
roadmap.notes: Each step is already designed in: new languages are one folder of strings, the leaf analyser is a plug-in interface, and districts and crops are edited in the admin screen.

arch.label: Architecture: phones talk to the web app, which calls the API. The API runs the advisory engine, stores data in the database, fetches weather from Open-Meteo and prices from Agmarknet, and pushes live alerts back to phones.
